DZCxiAMEYkK.content: 🚒 SUPPORT A LIVING WAGE FOR WILMINGTON FIREFIGHTERS 🚒 The City Manager's proposed budget includes something that should be common sense: a living wage for every Wilmington firefighter. Every day, firefighters respond to structure fires, medical emergencies, vehicle accidents, water rescues, hazardous materials incidents, and countless calls for help from our community. Our firefighters are proud to serve this community. DZGDELhNSOZ.content: Black Trumpet Farm is proud to be a Pledged Living Wage employer through Just Economics of Western NC. Just Economics calculates the actual cost of living in our region — housing, food, healthcare, transportation, childcare — and sets a wage floor based on what it really takes to live with dignity here. In 2026, that number is $24.10/hour for Buncombe County, based on what a single worker needs to qualify for a one-bedroom apartment. For context, NC's minimum wage is still $7.25. Just Economics certifies two levels of commitment. Fully certified employers pay at least $24.10/hour right now. Pledged employers pay a minimum of $20/hour and have made a binding public commitment to increase wages every year by 3% plus the annual rate of inflation until we reach full certification. When you buy from us at farmer's markets or through one of our restaurant partners, you're supporting a farm that takes this seriously. Our main goal is to grow quality, local food. But we believe a business can't truly be sustainable unless it sustains the people who make it possible. Thanks to everyone who buys local and supports our mission! #localfood #mushroomfarm# #asheville #livingwage

DZONe_kRZXz.content: 🚒 A Living Wage Changes Lives 🚒 "I love being a firefighter. There isn't a job in the world I'd rather do. But for years, my family and I have had to carefully budget every paycheck, work extra shifts, and sacrifice time together just to make ends meet. Like many firefighters, I've missed birthdays, ballgames, and family dinners because I needed overtime to provide for my family. That's time I'll never get back. This proposed living wage isn't about getting rich. It's about stability. It's about being able to pay the bills, save for the future, and spend more time with the people who matter most. It's about knowing that when I leave my family to answer the call, I can also provide for them at home. For the first time in a long time, I can see a future where I don't have to choose between serving my community and supporting my family. That's what a living wage means to me." Every firefighter has a story. Behind every uniform is a family that shares in the sacrifices of this profession. We are grateful for the City Manager's proposed budget that invests in the firefighters who serve Wilmington every day and helps ensure they can continue protecting this community while providing for their own families. @iaffofficial @pffp_nc @wectnews @wwaynews @portcitydaily #WilmingtonFirefighters #Local129 #LivingWage #SupportFirefighters #IAFF ProtectThoseWhoProtectYou WilmingtonNC FirefighterFamily PublicSafety StrongerTogether 🚒❤️

DZVy10bkkJX.content: Nearly 1 in 10 households in Calgary have a combined income of under $30,000. A family of four should receive $57,909 per year, while a single person should receive $28,954 to achieve a modest standard of living, according to the Market Basket Measure. VCC's Living Wage calculation for 2025 is $26.50/hr, which equates to $55,120 per year. When families don't make enough, they have to face impossible choices like skipping meals to avoid eviction or skipping medication to pay for food. VCC's poverty profiles share a snapshot of life in Calgary across each ward. While this data is from the 2021 census, it still provides an important look into life in Calgary and our progress towards poverty reduction. Swipe through to see how your ward compares and check out VCC' Poverty Profiles to learn more. We'll update this when data from the 2026 census becomes available. #YYC #Calgary #CalgaryNews #PovertyReduction #LivingWage
